comparison: Both evaluate simulated data experiments (C18-C19, C30-C31, C35-C36, C41). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED with statistically significant improvements (p<0.001), while peer reviewers also find solid evidence supporting the model's performance on simulated data. Strong agreement on simulated data results.

Both address comparative performance claims (C22, C57, C59, C69). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED with RTRBM outperforming cRBM on 4-6 out of 8 fish. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, noting 'marginal' improvements and one reviewer claiming RTRBM 'significantly underperforms' on temporal dynamics. Major disagreement on zebrafish performance.

Both evaluate down-sampling analysis and temporal resolution (C4, C67, C91). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED by Figure 4 results. Peer reviewers also find SUPPORTED, with no challenges to this methodological contribution. Strong agreement.

Both address clustering and spatial localization (C52, C79, plus C70/C80 in OpenEval). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED by clustering analysis in Figure 3D-E. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, explicitly challenging whether clusters are 'spatially localized,' calling it 'a stretch' especially for clusters 3 and 4. Significant disagreement.

Both evaluate main findings and temporal dynamics capture (C2, C68, plus C70/C80 in peer review). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED with quantitative improvements. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, questioning biological value and suggesting alternative methods could achieve similar insights. Disagreement on significance of contribution.

Both address transfer learning methodology (C20-C21, C61, C86-C87, C29). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED with successful training convergence. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, questioning methodological consistency and why cRBM wasn't used for synthetic data comparison. Disagreement on methodological choices.

Both discuss RTRBM architecture and temporal extensions (C24, C28, plus C14-C16 in OpenEval and C26 in peer review). OpenEval finds architectural claims SUPPORTED as well-established properties. Peer reviewers also find SUPPORTED, acknowledging it as 'a useful extension' with 'interesting feature.' Agreement on conceptual advance.

Both address sampling and temporal dynamics demonstration (C26). OpenEval finds claim SUPPORTED by Figure 1F showing sequential activation patterns. Peer reviewers also find related architectural claims SUPPORTED, acknowledging temporal modeling capability. Agreement.

Both address preprocessing and training methodology (C44, C46). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED with evidence of successful training. Peer reviewers also find SUPPORTED, requesting additional visualizations but not challenging the methodology itself. Agreement.

Both evaluate imaging limitations and motivational context (C76-C78, plus C13 in peer review). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED by citations and general knowledge. Peer reviewers also find SUPPORTED, acknowledging limitations of static models. Agreement on background motivation.

Both address empirical limitations and training challenges (C29, C86-C87). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED as honest technical assessments. Peer reviewers rate the broader methodological context UNCERTAIN, questioning why these limitations led to specific design choices. Partial disagreement on implications.

OpenEval evaluates transfer learning limitations (C88-C89) as UNCERTAIN, noting speculative nature about RBM conflating connections. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific limitation claims.
OpenEval evaluates single time-scale limitation and longer-timescale observations (C90, C92) as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these architectural limitations.
OpenEval evaluates computational efficiency claim (C71) as SUPPORTED based on empirical training time observations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

Both address prior work context (C12 overlaps, plus C1, C8-C11 in OpenEval). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED by citations to previous work. Peer reviewers also find motivational claims SUPPORTED. Agreement on background context.

Both evaluate background motivation (C13 overlaps, plus C5-C7 in OpenEval). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED by established literature. Peer reviewers also find SUPPORTED, acknowledging the gap in temporal modeling. Agreement.
OpenEval evaluates literature review claims (C17, C72-C75, C82) as SUPPORTED by multiple citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these literature context claims.
OpenEval evaluates comparative summary claim (C81) as SUPPORTED by Figures 2 and 3. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, though related performance claims are evaluated separately.

OpenEval evaluates design trade-offs (C83-C85) as SUPPORTED based on model architecture and ML principles. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific architectural trade-off claims.
OpenEval evaluates future work claims (C95-C99) as UNCERTAIN, noting speculative nature. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these forward-looking claims.
